Cape Gang Unit's Clipped wings

By: Michael Duffett | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
the blood of the innocent . a daily tragedy on the cape flats

Unique Selling Point:
Gang warfare  and killings of  innocent  people on the increase on the cape flats - especially since the army has gone  and the wings of the Anti-Gang Unit have been clipped

It’s thought that this recent spate of killings are revenge killings as a result of a kingpin gangster William Steven who was assassinated  in front of his home in Kraaifontein a few weeks ago  -  he headed up the  27’s gang.

It’s also thought that a major kingpin Yaganathan Pillay who was recently assassinated in Durban has had effects on all gangs in South Africa - he supplied guns and drugs.

In Mitchell’s Plain where 9 or so innocent people were gunned down, there are turf wars as some gangs encroach on the territory of the other gangs. These killings are dreadful because gangsters  are simply driving up roads and spraying the area with bullets - it’s though that gangsters are flexing their muscles by shooting innocent people in other gang territories.

What is going on, and why?


Summary:
Now Mitchells  Plain is fraught and has the following gangs:

Americans Young Americans/Ugly Americans) / HL’s/ Bad Boys/Fancy Boys/Nice Time Kids/ KGB’s/ Jires? Ghetto kids/ Mongrols/ Inglorius Bastards/ Mafais’s?
Spoilt Brats/ Sexy Boys/Dixie Boys .

Lyn Phillips is an activist in Mitchells Plain and works also for  local govt as a community development officer. She had great insight into gangs in the area where these 9 people were killed. She will organise two mothers to talk who lost children last week. She also runs a group which consists of other mothers  who have lost  children as a result of gangsterism in the area - and for years she and group have been going to protest at court..they don’t want alleged gangsters to get bail. She can provide a mother in the group  who can talk about her child who was first beaten by gangsters (have pictures) and then soon after assassinated - his crime? He did not want to join a gang.

Lyn is adamant  that since the AGU’s wings  were clipped, there has been an increase in gang warfare. There are posters that read - come back AGU.

Last year took detective from the AGU Charl Kinnear was murdered . Since then, the AGU spends its time providing security for AGU members. It no longer patrols every night, maybe once a week, no longer confiscates guns - it used to confiscate at least 15 a month. The fancy BMW’s that were donated to them at the beginning were taken away from them. General Lincoln is a very disillusioned man - I think he will appear on camera but may be limited by what he can say. But we can ask for statistics - and he will have to give them.

It would be a good idea to put questions to the WC Commissioner of SAPS who only recently said that a major issue is the number  of guns on the streets - where are they coming from?  Hello?
Questions must be put to him about the AGU.

Further information:
One person who believes that he has the answer is Neil Joubert, a larger than   life figure who recently broke away from the ANC (he was once a spy for MK where he was highly thought of - was President Ramaphosa’s advisor once) He has started a movement - united independent movement - and has 2.5 million followers. 18 months ago he started the CRU - that’s a community response unit made up of community members who started out providing support to police operations in a  township in Somerset - Lwandle. 56 members.  He says that during the period that he was there crime dropped by 72 per cent. This can be corroborated by the station commander, it seems. But the members of the unit do more than just prevent crime. They assist the community with food parcels, medical emergencies etc. . They get their hands dirty. They have patrolled on 187 days - and Neil has patrolled on 161 of those days.


Now that a memorandum was sent out by the police a few weeks back which prohibits security groups or even neighbourhood watches helping the police he is not allowed back to that township - and he says that the murder rate has gone up again.

One of the people in his group is a diminutive female  teacher who we can interview.  She gets into combat gear. He is checking. Neil is adamant that they are not a vigilante group and JP Smith has apparently termed them as the UBER of Security.

Now 4 members of a neighbourhood watch in Mitchells Plain has joined him for training and Neil wants to replicate in Mitchells Plain  what he is achieving in Somerset West. He says that community members must be empowered to stand up to the gangs. He says that it’s not only about fighting crime but endearing yourself to the community.

He is a quite a magnetic type of man I must admit. An orator. Apparently he gets death threats everyday but that does not concern him. He has loads of videos and pictures.

He has plenty  to say about SAPS - and the Anti gang unit - he is great friends with General Lincoln. He made a suggestion and its worthwhile researching this -how many generals are on suspension  at the moment or being investigated? - because SA has not the slightest chance of fighting crime if there is such dissent and division  in its ranks. 

Can go go, if you like this and we can do Table Mountain after this?

Michael

Script:


Mitchells Plain on the Cape Flats. While people just try to make a living here, gangs seem to have the upper hand. Police statistics show the area has the third highest prevalence of illegal firearms in the country. In 2020 it recorded a hundred and fifteen murders.

The last thing Janet Swart wanted was for her grandson who lived with her and three other grandchildren, to join the statistics. Tamir Mitchell loved to dance. He was the apple of her eye.

Janet (00:26):
He was like my baby boy in the house. And everybody just say that I spoiled him because I love him

LINK
On the 25th of February this year, 13 year old Tamir Mitchell was standing here on Cadillac street, beacon Valley at around 8:30 at night. When a car approached from that direction, apparently a white Chevrolet. It drew up and a volume of shots, rang out

Janet (01:08):
And people shout but it's Tamir laying there. When I got there, his eye was shot out, he was, I couldn't handle seeing him like that. It was horrible.

Derek (01:22):
He was shot many times?

Janet (01:23):
He was shot 23 times.

LINK (01:28):
Further up the road lived 18 year old Morgan Munnik. His mother Melanie said that he lived for soccer and was loved by his peers.

Derek (01:37):
What did he dream of doing with his life?

Melanie (01:40):
He wanted to be a professional soccer player....

Derek (01:41):
A professional soccer player.

VO (01:45):
She also heard distant gunfire that night.

LINK (01:49):
The gangsters continued along Cadillac street and just a few hundred meters away opened fire again. This time claiming the life of young Morgan Munnik, an only child.

VO (02:02):
She found her son lying on the street, mortally wounded.

Melanie (02:14):
And when I got to my son he was just lying there, there was a little heartbeat, a little breath. So it's almost like he was just waiting for us to come....

Derek (02:25):
Did you manage, to say goodbye?

Melanie (02:29):
The last thing that I can remember that the tears was rolling down his face. It's almost like he was saying goodbye to me.

VO (02:40):
Several other children were hit by bullets, but they are recovering

LINK (02:46):
Just two days later on the 27th of February, a Saturday morning, a car stopped over there. Three gangsters got out and walked across this field and randomly opened fire on a group of neighbours sitting outside this house in tafelsig. Four people died

VO (03:06):
Soon after these killings, the Western Cape provincial minister of Community safety Fritz visited the bereaved families. His sources said these could be revenge killings.

Fritz (03:26):
do you remember when the alleged gangster was killed? Um, in, in Kraaifontein, Scottsville, which is another hot spot, Kraaifontein is a hotspot, two policemen were killed the last week. So when that happened, it seemed as if they just came, this side into Mitchell's Plain and randomly shot into the territory of another gang.

VO: The motives for these apparently random killings have not been established, but Mitchells Plain anti-gang activist Lynn Phillips knows how gangs operate.

Lynn:
Its all because of drug turf, its all because of tryig to initiate young people to gangs, they need to showcase their worth to the gang leaders in order for them to become part of the gang.

According to Phillips there are over 20 gangs operating in Mitchells and its suburbs

LINK (03:50):



VO (04:23):
All these mothers have lost children to gang violence – Philips started the THIS group some years ago to provide mutual support and make their voices heard at court where they demand that gangsters be denied bail. Lorraine Lawrence joined after her son paid the ultimate price for not joining a gang.

Lorraine (04:46):
He was a very loving person. When ever he sees everyone in the road, he would always greet them, hug them and ask them. How are you?

VO (04:56):
BRANDON had a good job and was set for a bright future. Lawrence SAID that gangsters were envious of him and tried to force him to join the gang. He refused.. and in APRIL 2020 they assaulted him. He refused to lay charges.

Lorraine (05:13):
He said, mommy, no. If I go like charges, they will probably kill me.

VO (05:19):
3 months later, he was ambushed and killed on the street.

Lorraine (05:24):
I just took the, the, the, the blanket that was on him. I took it off and I wanted to make sure if it's my son that was laying there and I saw him just laying there. I couldn't even cry...

Derek (05:45):
How many times was he shot?

Lorraine (05:46):
He was shot 14 times.

Derek. (05:47):
14?

Lorraine (05:47):
14 times he was shot

VO (05:53):
In a tragic twist of fate, Brandon died on the same day his father had, 23 years ago. He had been a gangster and was murdered for trying to leave the gang.

In 2018, to much acclaim, the police’s anti-gang unit was launched in Cape Town. IN 2019 we joined them on a raid as they implemented their mission to crack down on gangers and their illicit ECONOMIES In the first month of operation they arrested 120 suspects. 35 of those were gang leaders. Phillips felt the unit was making inroads.

Lynn:
There was this fear from gangsters that there is a unit that really looks after the community and that they feared that unit at the time. Today, we don’t see them any longer.

VO:
Sources say it was the murder of the unit’s top investigator Lt Charl Kinnear, last September that sparked the anti-gang unit’s diminishing presence in Mitchells Plain – now it mostly uses its members to provide security for fellow police members.


Fritz:
A lot of us hasn’t seen them but it would be good to have them back.

(Waiting for SAPS reply)

The police declined an interview but in response to our questions they that ….OPERATIONAL DEPLOYMENTS BY THE ANTI GANG UNUT CONTINUE AS GUIDED BY THE CRIME PATTERN ANAYLSIS,,,,AND THAT OPERATIONS ON AN ONGOING BASIS ARE CONDUCTED.

IN THE LAST 5 MONTHS THE MITCHELLS POLICE HAVE CONFISCATED 29 ILLEGAL FIREARMS AND ARRESTED
17 PEOPLE.



The Western Cape Provincial Government has adopted a safety plan, which aims to halve the murder rate in the province in ten years’ time, through law enforcement and violence prevention interventions – which hinges on community involvement.

Fritz (07:35):
Civil society must also get organized. Civil society must also form into neighborhood watches and maybe this mustn't become the domain of a few. It must become the representatives and people joining of all people

VO
In recent weeks, members of a volunteer group in Mitchells Plain started training with a private community response unit from Somerset West that was founded by a man called Neil de Beer. Formerly involved in apartheid’s security police, De Beer then BECAME AN ANC spy. He now has political ambitions and has STARTED the United Independent Movement. His home in SOMERSET WEST is not FAR FROM MITCHELLS PLAIN.

NEIL:
There's a borderline between vigilantism and community protection. And I think it was time for me to get up in my local informal settlement and my community in the helderberg to say enough of crime. Enough. And we have to get up as a community and act.

VO (08:26):
De Beer’s Community Response Units patrol on their own and have provided back UP to police operations in the township of LWANDLE in Somerset West. The members come from the community. To date they've undertaken 171 night operations and claim a success rate of a 70 per cent drop in crime.

Derek (09:38):
Are you thinking of taking that formula to Mitchell's plan?

de Beer (09:43):
I'm not thinking. I am. It's time that we also spread the winning concept of a community-based reaction unit.

VO
These Mitchells Plain men, 2 are fed-up with gang are eager to replicate the unit’s winning formula back home.


VO (09:56):
In the meantime, Janet is struggling to get over the loss of Tamir. Hundreds of grieving community members attended his funeral.

Janet (10:09):
I'm still seeing him coming in. I'm still waiting for him. I still forget and go buy stuff that I must buy for him because I keep on forgot that he is not here with us anymore.
VO (10:24):
Melanie is devastated.
Melanie (10:32):
He was in my life for 18 years and I can't just put that aside.
VO (10:38):
Lorraine still can't believe that her SON is gone.
LINK (10:43):
Tragically for now this is the reality of life in Mitchell's Plain.

He had been a gangster and was murdered for trying to leave the gang. In 2018, to much acclaim, the police’s anti-gang unit was launched in Cape Town. IN 2019 we joined them on a raid as they implemented their mission to crack down on gangers and their illicit ECONOMIES In the first month of operation they arrested 120 suspects. 35 of those were gang leaders. Phillips felt the unit was making inroads. Lynn: There was this fear from gangsters that there is a unit that really looks after the community and that they feared that unit at the time. Today, we don’t see them any longer. VO: Sources say it was the murder of the unit’s top investigator Lt Charl Kinnear, last September that sparked the anti-gang unit’s diminishing presence in Mitchells Plain – now it mostly uses its members to provide security for fellow police members. Fritz: A lot of us hasn’t seen them but it would be good to have them back. (Waiting for SAPS reply) The police declined an interview but in response to our questions they that ….OPERATIONAL DEPLOYMENTS BY THE ANTI GANG UNUT CONTINUE AS GUIDED BY THE CRIME PATTERN ANAYLSIS,,,,AND THAT OPERATIONS ON AN ONGOING BASIS ARE CONDUCTED. IN THE LAST 5 MONTHS THE MITCHELLS POLICE HAVE CONFISCATED 29 ILLEGAL FIREARMS AND ARRESTED 17 PEOPLE. The Western Cape Provincial Government has adopted a safety plan, which aims to halve the murder rate in the province in ten years’ time, through law enforcement and violence prevention interventions – which hinges on community involvement. Fritz (07:35): Civil society must also get organized. Civil society must also form into neighborhood watches and maybe this mustn't become the domain of a few. It must become the representatives and people joining of all people VO In recent weeks, members of a volunteer group in Mitchells Plain started training with a private community response unit from Somerset West that was founded by a man called Neil de Beer. Formerly involved in apartheid’s security police, De Beer then BECAME AN ANC spy. He now has political ambitions and has STARTED the United Independent Movement. His home in SOMERSET WEST is not FAR FROM MITCHELLS PLAIN. NEIL: There's a borderline between vigilantism and community protection. And I think it was time for me to get up in my local informal settlement and my community in the helderberg to say enough of crime. Enough. And we have to get up as a community and act. VO (08:26): De Beer’s Community Response Units patrol on their own and have provided back UP to police operations in the township of LWANDLE in Somerset West. The members come from the community. To date they've undertaken 171 night operations and claim a success rate of a 70 per cent drop in crime. Derek (09:38): Are you thinking of taking that formula to Mitchell's plan? de Beer (09:43): I'm not thinking. I am. It's time that we also spread the winning concept of a community-based reaction unit. VO These Mitchells Plain men, 2 are fed-up with gang are eager to replicate the unit’s winning formula back home. VO (09:56): In the meantime, Janet is struggling to get over the loss of Tamir. Hundreds of grieving community members attended his funeral. Janet (10:09): I'm still seeing him coming in. I'm still waiting for him. I still forget and go buy stuff that I must buy for him because I keep on forgot that he is not here with us anymore. VO (10:24): Melanie is devastated. Melanie (10:32): He was in my life for 18 years and I can't just put that aside. VO (10:38): Lorraine still can't believe that her SON is gone. LINK (10:43): Tragically for now this is the reality of life in Mitchell's Plain. Disclaimer

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): the blood of the innocent . a daily tragedy on the cape flats
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Gang warfare and killings of innocent people on the increase on the cape flats - especially since the army has gone and the wings of the Anti-Gang Unit have been clipped It’s thought that this recent spate of killings are revenge killings as a result of a kingpin gangster William Steven who was assassinated in front of his home in Kraaifontein a few weeks ago - he headed up the 27’s gang. It’s also thought that a major kingpin Yaganathan Pillay who was recently assassinated in Durban has had effects on all gangs in South Africa - he supplied guns and drugs. In Mitchell’s Plain where 9 or so innocent people were gunned down, there are turf wars as some gangs encroach on the territory of the other gangs. These killings are dreadful because gangsters are simply driving up roads and spraying the area with bullets - it’s though that gangsters are flexing their muscles by shooting innocent people in other gang territories. What is going on, and why?
metadata.Summary: Now Mitchells Plain is fraught and has the following gangs: Americans Young Americans/Ugly Americans) / HL’s/ Bad Boys/Fancy Boys/Nice Time Kids/ KGB’s/ Jires? Ghetto kids/ Mongrols/ Inglorius Bastards/ Mafais’s? Spoilt Brats/ Sexy Boys/Dixie Boys . Lyn Phillips is an activist in Mitchells Plain and works also for local govt as a community development officer. She had great insight into gangs in the area where these 9 people were killed. She will organise two mothers to talk who lost children last week. She also runs a group which consists of other mothers who have lost children as a result of gangsterism in the area - and for years she and group have been going to protest at court..they don’t want alleged gangsters to get bail. She can provide a mother in the group who can talk about her child who was first beaten by gangsters (have pictures) and then soon after assassinated - his crime? He did not want to join a gang. Lyn is adamant that since the AGU’s wings were clipped, there has been an increase in gang warfare. There are posters that read - come back AGU. Last year took detective from the AGU Charl Kinnear was murdered . Since then, the AGU spends its time providing security for AGU members. It no longer patrols every night, maybe once a week, no longer confiscates guns - it used to confiscate at least 15 a month. The fancy BMW’s that were donated to them at the beginning were taken away from them. General Lincoln is a very disillusioned man - I think he will appear on camera but may be limited by what he can say. But we can ask for statistics - and he will have to give them. It would be a good idea to put questions to the WC Commissioner of SAPS who only recently said that a major issue is the number of guns on the streets - where are they coming from? Hello? Questions must be put to him about the AGU.
metadata.Further information: One person who believes that he has the answer is Neil Joubert, a larger than life figure who recently broke away from the ANC (he was once a spy for MK where he was highly thought of - was President Ramaphosa’s advisor once) He has started a movement - united independent movement - and has 2.5 million followers. 18 months ago he started the CRU - that’s a community response unit made up of community members who started out providing support to police operations in a township in Somerset - Lwandle. 56 members. He says that during the period that he was there crime dropped by 72 per cent. This can be corroborated by the station commander, it seems. But the members of the unit do more than just prevent crime. They assist the community with food parcels, medical emergencies etc. . They get their hands dirty. They have patrolled on 187 days - and Neil has patrolled on 161 of those days. Now that a memorandum was sent out by the police a few weeks back which prohibits security groups or even neighbourhood watches helping the police he is not allowed back to that township - and he says that the murder rate has gone up again. One of the people in his group is a diminutive female teacher who we can interview. She gets into combat gear. He is checking. Neil is adamant that they are not a vigilante group and JP Smith has apparently termed them as the UBER of Security. Now 4 members of a neighbourhood watch in Mitchells Plain has joined him for training and Neil wants to replicate in Mitchells Plain what he is achieving in Somerset West. He says that community members must be empowered to stand up to the gangs. He says that it’s not only about fighting crime but endearing yourself to the community. He is a quite a magnetic type of man I must admit. An orator. Apparently he gets death threats everyday but that does not concern him. He has loads of videos and pictures. He has plenty to say about SAPS - and the Anti gang unit - he is great friends with General Lincoln. He made a suggestion and its worthwhile researching this -how many generals are on suspension at the moment or being investigated? - because SA has not the slightest chance of fighting crime if there is such dissent and division in its ranks. Can go go, if you like this and we can do Table Mountain after this? Michael
